name: California
summary_text: Highest legal floor in the country: the first sanctuary-state law for transgender care (SB 107, signed 2022) and shield protections against out-of-state enforcement. But also the most recorded incidents of any state in 2025 (198, GLAAD ALERT), a "dramatic increase" in Los Angeles hate-crime reports, and 34 recorded killings of trans women 2008–2025 (4.1 per 100k). Above the national score 0.36; law and street volume pull opposite ways.

sources.title: GLAAD ALERT DESK DOCUMENTS MORE THAN 1,000 ANTI-LGBTQ INCIDENTS NATIONWIDE IN 2025 | GLAAD
sources.claim_summary: GLAAD ALERT Desk press release (27 January 2026): 1,042 anti-LGBTQ incidents across 47 states plus DC in 2025, up 5% on 2024's 984; 51% of incidents targeted transgender and gender-nonconforming people, a 10-point increase on 2024, with June 2025 up nearly 400% since tracking began in June 2022. Per the research dossier, the desk recorded 198 incidents in California — the most of any state.

sources.title: Over 1,000 anti-LGBTQ+ attacks occurred in 2025: report | Advocate.com
sources.claim_summary: The Advocate report (27 January 2026) on the GLAAD ALERT data: 2025 was "one of the most dangerous years on record" for LGBTQ Americans, with the 1,042-incident national total and law-enforcement data showing a dramatic increase in anti-LGBTQ hate crime in Los Angeles over the same period.

sources.title: Safe States Don’t Make People Safer
sources.claim_summary: The Needle investigation (16 July 2026): a state-by-state analysis of TGEU Trans Murder Monitoring killings of trans women 2008–2025 set against each state's legal-risk tier; every figure is an undercounted floor. California sits in the safest-law group yet records 34 killings (4.1 per 100k trans women/yr) — the article's headline finding is that legal risk does not predict lethal risk ("Safe States Don't Make People Safer").

sources.title: California Becomes First Sanctuary State for Transgender Youth Seeking Medical Care | KQED
sources.claim_summary: KQED report (18 October 2022, updated February 2025): California became the first US "sanctuary state" for transgender youth — Governor Newsom signed SB 107 in September 2022, guaranteeing access to gender-affirming care for people coming from other states and shielding families and providers from out-of-state child-abuse investigations and criminal prosecution; the law faced opposition from conservatives and faith-based groups.
